name: critical_delivery_20261105
comment: D32 section 6 / D33 (FQ-143): one CRITICAL event reaches three channels, and only the operator's allowlist reaches the text one.
What the suite asserts: there is no second class list in code (the taxonomy is read from config/critical_text_classes.json,
and its absence refuses rather than opening the channel); a class outside the taxonomy is refused before anything is sent;
a disabled class loses its text and still goes by email and the Critical chat; the text guard has no override argument,
which the suite pins by inspecting the signature; every gateway address on file is a target, a non-address is refused
rather than dialled, and the contact file is read from the private persistent-state root, never from this public repository;
one event produces a receipt per channel; a failed or unconfigured channel is a receipt and never stops the others;
DELIVERED means at least one channel confirmed; no receipt carries an address; and the text message leads with the action.
What it does NOT assert: queuing to a durable outbox, retry with backoff, acknowledgement stopping repeats, and the

operator-facing hourly summary. Those are the next slice of FQ-143 and nothing here claims them. The producer gate (FQ-150/D35) checks that all twelve class ids have a producer, that B4's action carries the full https reauth link with no dev port and never asks the operator to reply with a code, and that the dry run produces every enabled class with fakes. The ack gate checks that the first acknowledgement records who and when, that a second changes nothing, that the statement only claims an unacknowledged row so two racers cannot both win, and that a missing durable store is reported rather than claimed as success.
